warmup.text: The wind has died. The ship sits still on the sea, day after day. Two men think they are ruined. Before you read, think: can one problem ever be the answer to another?

words.text: Use the roots to work out words, and use the tags in your own scene. In the game, six more narrows. Two channels test speech spellings from today's chapter.

reading.text: Read Chapter 6. Reread one funny part and take it apart: the setup, then the turn. Then notice who thinks of the potato idea, and who gets the credit.

assignment.text: Three questions, the last one about all three chapters. Then revise your scene with the checklist. Make sure each new speaker gets a new paragraph.

game.title: Through the Strait
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 narrows today
game.look: Your ship sails west through the Strait of Magellan, a narrow passage at the bottom of South America. At each narrows, tap the channel with the word that really fits. Each narrows you pass lights a fire on Tierra del Fuego, the Land of Fire.

do: Read the clue at the narrows.
Look at the word in each channel.
Tap the channel with the word that really fits.
Tap Sail on.
how.why: A root only helps if it is really there, and a speech spelling only works if the apostrophe is in the right place.

game.doneLine: The Pacific is open. Come back tomorrow for six more narrows.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lus (play): hard to catch, always slipping away.
narrows.why: e (out) + lus (play) + ive. Exclusive comes from clus, which means shut.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lus (play): a false belief, as if your mind were being tricked.
narrows.why: de + lus + ion. Dilution means making something weaker with water.

narrows.clue: Find the word with ris (laugh): able to make people laugh.
narrows.why: ris + ible: laughable. Visible comes from vis, which means see.

narrows.clue: Find the word with lud (play): a short break between the acts of a play.
narrows.why: inter (between) + lude (play). Interval has no play root.

narrows.clue: Chapter 6: Mountain Jim says the haircut needs evening up on one side. Which spelling is his?
narrows.why: evenin' = evening. The apostrophe stands where the g was.
narrows.miss: Where is the letter that is missing? Put the apostrophe there.

narrows.clue: Chapter 6: asked if he will eat the shark, Mountain Jim says he sure will. Which spelling shows how he says sure?
narrows.why: shore is how he says sure. A sound changes but no letter is left out, so there is no apostrophe.
narrows.miss: Is anything missing, or is a sound just changed?

virtue.name: self-control
virtue.title: The self-control meter
virtue.intro: Think about one moment from Chapter 6.
virtue.moment: Jack thinks of the potato idea. But Praiseworthy tells the two men the idea is so simple that “a boy could have thought of it.” Jack remained silent, but stuck his hands in his pockets and felt proud of himself.
virtue.ask: How much self-control does Jack show here? Slide to show.
virtue.take: Mason's take: a lot. Jack could have shouted that it was his idea. He kept quiet and let the good news belong to the two men.

art.title: Calm Early Evening Sea
art.alt: A painting of a two-masted sailing ship sitting still on a glassy sea under big white clouds, with a few people and a boat on the shore.
art.look: Ivan Aivazovsky painted this calm in 1884, far from South America. Not a breath of wind moves the sails, and the sea is as flat as glass. In Chapter 6 the Lady Wilma sits like this for weeks off the coast of Chile, with no coal left to turn her paddlewheels.
